title: What Are the Chinese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Publish method: update in place, change slug and path to /expert-advice/chinese-wedding-traditions, confirm the old URL returns a 301. Check for duplicate Chinese pages (tea ceremony, Real Weddings) to 301 or cross-link. Protect its rankings.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch (retry with a render wait if no body), records its 6 headings and errors; SEO pulls its ranked keywords (US and AU), checks duplicate Chinese pages, and the outline keeps covering every query with real volume. Drop the 'weird' framing; describe customs respectfully. Keep sourceable traditions; never reuse wording; drop errors. Never refer to an 'old version' of the page in the copy.
DIVERSITY: customs vary by region and community (Cantonese, Hokkien, Teochew and others; diaspora in Australia, Singapore, Malaysia). Say so once, tie a custom to a region only where a source does.
Culture, not politics: no commentary on Hong Kong, Taiwan or other political questions; place names as sources give them, used neutrally.

Likely customs (brief finalises): Three Letters and Six Rites; betrothal gifts (guo da li) with no amounts; auspicious date; hair-combing ceremony; door games at the bride's home; tea ceremony; red and the double happiness character; dragon and phoenix; qun kwa and bridal dress where sourced; red envelopes (hongbao) with no amounts; the wedding banquet; the bride's return visit. Superstitions described lightly.
UNESCO only where its own text links an element to weddings (for example Traditional tea processing techniques and associated social practices in China, 2022). Confirm each page live and its title.

Destination angle: Smartraveller China checked live (level and any higher-level areas; risks stated neutrally as Smartraveller words them). Legal from official sources only: Australian Embassy Beijing and consulates (CNI, notarial), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (recognition), Chinese civil affairs registration only if an official page can be read; otherwise 'check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'. Chinese-Australian weddings at home are a strong angle.

Sources: UNESCO, national and state museums (Palace Museum, Hong Kong Museum of History, Chinese Museum Melbourne, Powerhouse), encyclopaedias, academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' with no meanings as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker. One honest framing line per section.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (tea set, red envelopes) labelled illustrative pending approval; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: betrothal and wedding-day rites; B: symbols, dress, banquet, UNESCO and legal), 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.

Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts (no betrothal or red-envelope sums); no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
